newsitem.title: USA: Eastman confirms 10-pct sales growth goal.
newsitem.headline: Eastman confirms 10-pct sales growth goal.

text.p: An Eastman Chemical Co executive Tuesdsay reiterated Eastman's goal of achieving annual sales revenue growth of 10 percent.

Looking to the year 2000, vice chairman and executive vice president R. Wiley Bourne, Jr., told institutional investors at the Merrill Lynch Chemical Conference that he expects to see revenue growth in each of the company's three segments.
Core Plastics generated about $1.4 billion of Eastman's sales in 1996, the company said. Through the year 2000, the company said, it expects Core Plastics to grow eight to 11 percent a year.
Much of that growth is likely to come from growth in volume for EASTAPAK PET polyester packaging plastic, due to increasing demand and additional available capacity, the company said.
Chemical Intermediates accounted for approximately $700 million of Eastman's 1996 sales, the company said.

With expected strong demand growth in markets such as laminates for safety glass, plasticizers for floor coverings and medical devices, and chemicals for artificial sweeteners and agricultural uses, Bourne said annual revenue for Chemical Intermediates is expected to grow six to eight percent.
The Specialty and Performance segment is Eastman's largest and most diverse segment, and generated revenues of about $2.6 billion in 1996, the company said.
According to Bourne, with the exception of fiber products, many of the product lines in this segment are growing at or above 10 percent annually.
"Specialty and Performance is expected to grow eight to 10 percent over the next four years," he said.
